title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the surrounding pages Grothendieck develops 'L-groups': discrete or profinite groups equipped with an 'L-structure', a distinguished family of conjugacy classes of procyclic 'loop' subgroups (lacets), which model the inertia or peripheral subgroups at cusps. On the previous page he proposes to characterise them by the condition that the centraliser of every finite-index subgroup is trivial, then to treat the general case by extensions by finite groups, and to define 'L-Galois topoi'.

This page opens with a methodological claim. The right general setting for defining and studying general Teichmüller groups may be L-groups rather than 'groups with loops' (groupes à lacets).

The test case is (4): Γ^+_{0,3} ≅ PSL(2,Z), described as a fundamental group 'π_1(M_{0,3}(C), S_3; −J)'. The next page makes the meaning clear through the extension 1 → Π_{0,3} → Γ^+_{0,3} → Γ_3 (= S_3) → 1. Here:
- Π_{0,3} is the free group of rank 2, i.e. π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}), which is Γ(2)/{±1};
- the quotient by S_3 is the j-line, viewed as an orbifold (stack);
- so Γ^+_{0,3} is the orbifold fundamental group of the j-line.

The L-structure is the single conjugacy class of the cusp-stabiliser (parabolic) subgroup. It can be generated by ε_0 = (1 −1; 0 1) or equivalently by ε_1 = (1 0; 1 1). These generate conjugate subgroups, since S T⁻¹ S⁻¹ = (1 0; 1 1) with T = (1 1; 0 1). So the class is indeed unique.

The property he calls 'remarkable' concerns the discrete L-group. Every L-automorphism that is 'direct' (acts trivially on the orientation module, i.e. sends the loop generator to a conjugate of itself rather than of its inverse) is inner. In modern terms, Out(PSL(2,Z)) = Z/2, generated by conjugation by diag(1,−1) ∈ GL(2,Z). That automorphism preserves the parabolic class but sends T to T⁻¹, so it is the orientation-reversing one. Hence direct L-automorphisms are inner, and the claim holds.

He then conjectures that this property, together with trivial centre (or better, trivial centralisers of all finite-index subgroups), characterises the group up to non-unique isomorphism. The next page puts a hat on the group, i.e. refers to the profinite completion Γ̂^+_{0,3}. His proposed strategy there is to show that every automorphism preserves Π̂_{0,3}. The supporting lemma is that every surjection Γ̂^+_{0,3} = Ẑ/2 ⨿ Ẑ/3 → S_3 is conjugate to the canonical one. This lemma is correct: the generators must go to a transposition and a 3-cycle, and S_3 acts simply transitively on the 6 such pairs.
errors:
In the profinite setting announced on the next page ('tout L-aut de Γ̂^+_{0,3} est intérieur'), the statement appears false.
- G_Q acts on π_1^et(M_{1,1,Q̄}) ≅ SL(2,Z)^, hence on Γ̂^+_{0,3}.
- Elements of Gal(Q̄/Q^ab) act trivially on the orientation module (trivial cyclotomic character) and preserve the cusp-inertia class, so they are direct L-automorphisms.
- If such an element acted innerly, it would act innerly on Π̂_{0,3} = π_1(P^1 − 3 points): the canonical S_3-quotient is preserved and S_3 has trivial centre.
- This contradicts Belyi's faithfulness theorem.
More generally the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT acts by such automorphisms (cf. Minamide–Nakamura on automorphisms of profinite braid groups). Grothendieck's insertion '(discret)' on this page suggests he may have restricted the claim to the discrete group.

As stated, the characterisation conjecture (direct L-automorphisms inner + trivial centre or trivial centralisers ⇒ ≅ PSL(2,Z)) is insufficient even for discrete L-groups. Other one-cusp triangle groups (p,q,∞) with p ≠ q, e.g. the Hecke group (2,4,∞), have trivial centre, trivial finite-index centralisers, a single cusp class, and only inner direct peripheral-preserving automorphisms. By Dehn–Nielsen–Baer this reduces to the triviality of the orbifold mapping class group. Extra hypotheses would be needed (e.g. on the torsion, or on the S_3-quotient used on the next page).
The notation 'π_1(M_{0,3}(C), S_3; −J)' is unclear. The group is the orbifold π_1 of M_{0,4}/S_3 (the j-line), and the meaning of '−J' (base point?) is not explained on this page.

ideas.what: Teichmüller groups should be studied as L-groups: groups with a structure of conjugacy classes of loop/inertia subgroups, discrete or profinite.
ideas.modern_name: Groups with peripheral structure / profinite groups with inertia (cuspidal) structure; peripherally-preserving outer automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Peripheral structures: classical (Dehn–Nielsen–Baer). Profinite inertia/cuspidal structure: Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi (1990s–2010s).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions Teichmüller groups and the Teichmüller tower; 'L-groups' are specific to the Longue Marche manuscripts.

ideas.what: PSL(2,Z) as the orbifold π_1 of the j-line, an extension of S_3 by the free group π_1(P^1 − 3 points), with its unique class of parabolic (cusp) subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of M_{1,1} modulo ±1; Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL(2,Z) with quotient S_3
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower in genus 0 and 1, PSL(2,Z)), in spirit

ideas.what: Every direct (orientation-preserving) L-automorphism of discrete PSL(2,Z) is inner.
ideas.modern_name: Out(PSL(2,Z)) = Z/2 realised by GL(2,Z); analogue of Ivanov's theorem for mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for PSL(2,Z); Ivanov (1988) for mapping class groups

ideas.what: Conjecture that 'direct L-automorphisms inner' plus trivial centraliser of every finite-index subgroup characterises Γ̂^+_{0,3} up to non-unique isomorphism.
ideas.modern_name: Group-theoretic characterisation / rigidity of profinite Teichmüller groups; profinite anabelian reconstruction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related work: Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki; Minamide–Nakamura (automorphisms of profinite braid groups)

ideas.what: Lemma (next page): every surjection Γ̂^+_{0,3} → S_3 is conjugate to the canonical one, so Π̂_{0,3} is characteristic.
ideas.modern_name: Characteristic-ness of the congruence subgroup Γ(2)^ in PSL(2,Z)^ = Ẑ/2 ⨿ Ẑ/3

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes axiomatising general Teichmüller groups as L-groups (groups with loop-class structure), and characterising PSL(2,Z) or its profinite completion intrinsically by an 'every direct L-automorphism is inner' rigidity plus centraliser triviality. This axiomatic programme was not developed in his published texts, though profinite anabelian work on cuspidal or inertia subgroups and the automorphism groups of profinite braid and mapping class groups covers related ground.
missed.quote: Il se pourrait que le "bon" contexte général pour définir et étudier des groupes de Teichmüller généraux soit celui des L-groupes, plutôt que celui des groupes à lacets.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precursor to the group-theoretic reconstruction of inertia and cuspidal structures (Mochizuki, Hoshi) and to the computation of Out of profinite braid and mapping class groups (Minamide–Nakamura). It also documents a moment where the discrete rigidity was apparently expected to pass to the profinite setting, which fails because of the Galois/GT action.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a programmatic note with a correct classical fact about discrete PSL(2,Z) and an imprecise characterisation conjecture. Historically interesting is the apparent expectation (next page) that the profinite completion also has only inner direct L-automorphisms; this contradicts Belyi and the GT action, and the inserted '(discret)' may be a later correction. No new finished result.
transcription_corrections: 'ou plutôt[?] L_1 engendré par ε_1' should likely read 'ou par L_1 engendré par ε_1': the parabolic class can be defined by either generator.
'π_1(\mathcal{M}_{0,3}(\mathbb{C}), \mathfrak{S}_3; -J)': the symbol read as M may be a script U or M. The meaning (orbifold quotient by S_3 with a base point '−J'?) is uncertain from the image.
'(discret)' is an insertion above 'a la', qualifying 'Le L-groupe (discret)'. It is correctly placed in the transcription and is mathematically significant.
